assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) made it broadly applicable. Its use is visible in countless total syntheses, medicinal chemistry programs and process routes, which is the clearest case on the list of a method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds. It is the natural complement to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and the new chemistry (amine coordination, deprotonation, reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes) is clear.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination and ligand systems and are the dominant figures; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was a precursor with narrower scope. A two-person prize is clean; the Kosugi/Migita precedent is a minor priority question.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and heavy industrial adoption. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Weight of the Kosugi and Migita precursor work relative to the catalytic general method
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may weigh against it for some members

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of reactivity for synthesis, generating radicals and radical ions under mild conditions from simple catalysts, and enabled bond constructions that were difficult by polar chemistry. It is widely adopted in academic and pharmaceutical synthesis, including dual catalysis with nickel. Conceptually the manifold is simple and transferable.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across at least seven people. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, so I would not re-center on him. Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced key synthetic applications around 2008-2012; Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre have earlier or complementary claims. Any three-person configuration leaves clear omissions.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough, with a decade and more of broad use and industrial application. Some of the field is still incremental, so the core discovery must be separated from later applications.
uncertainties: Prior MacMillan recognition may complicate the framing
Reductions to a single concept versus a field of related methods

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalyst-controlled C-H functionalization changes the logic of retrosynthesis by treating C-H bonds as functional handles. Ligand-enabled Pd(II) catalysis and directing-group and template strategies allow site-selective transformations, including remote positions. It is increasingly used in late-stage functionalization and in synthesis planning, though routine adoption is less universal than cross-coupling.
assessment.attribution: Yu is the most compelling for ligand- and template-control of selectivity and Sanford for Pd(II/IV) mechanism and fluorination and related methods. Hartwig (listed here too) is better placed under B011, and Daugulis and Smith have earlier priority contributions, so credit is contested at the edges.
assessment.maturity: Highly active field with strong independent validation, but the scope is still evolving and a prize now could be seen as slightly early compared with cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Breadth of practical adoption versus demonstration scope

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid and base combinations activate H2 and other small molecules without a metal. This was a surprising conceptual shift in main-group reactivity, leading to metal-free hydrogenation catalysis and a family of new reactions. The chemistry is original and clear, even if its practical impact is smaller than for transition-metal methods.
assessment.attribution: Stephan (2006 H2 activation by a phosphonium borate) and Erker (intramolecular and related FLP systems, later work on reactivity scope) are the clear pair, a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Nearly two decades of confirmation and wide expansion. Industrial uptake remains limited, which tempers the case.
uncertainties: Limited industrial and synthetic adoption so far
Relative weight of the Welch and Stephan 2006 discovery versus Erker's contributions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes made persistent carbenes a new class of ligand and organocatalyst. N-heterocyclic carbenes underpin modern olefin metathesis catalysts and many Pd and other metal systems, while Bertrand's cyclic alkyl amino carbenes extended reactivity. The structural and bonding insights are fundamental and impact on catalysis is large.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 crystalline imidazol-2-ylidene is the decisive first isolation; Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbene and later CAAC work are major. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are application-side contributors and are less central.
assessment.maturity: Mature with more than 30 years of use. Part of the impact is already tied to the 2005 metathesis prize, which could count against it.
uncertainties: Overlap in impact with the 2005 metathesis prize
Bertrand's early carbenes versus Arduengo's priority

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation gave chemists a chemoselective way to join unprotected peptide segments, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine in practice. The chemical idea is simple and general, and it has enabled modified proteins, mirror-image proteins and site-specific studies of post-translational modifications.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original NCL (1994 paper with Dawson, Muir, Clark-Lewis, Kent). Muir is central for expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu contributed extensions and applications, so six names compete for three slots.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use. Recognition is well-timed, though some would consider the method specialized compared with broad bond-forming reactions.
uncertainties: Division of credit between synthetic ligation and semisynthesis (EPL)
Whether the method counts as widely routine outside specialist labs

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made fast, high-yielding automated DNA synthesis possible and underlies oligonucleotides for PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and therapeutics. It is a prime example of a synthetic method becoming invisible infrastructure, and the chemical logic (stable phosphoramidites activated by tetrazole, iterative cycle) is elegant.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite approach (Beaucage and Caruthers 1981) and is the decisive figure. Hood is credited for automation instrumentation, which is not the chemical discovery, so I would propose a single laureate; others who worked on earlier phosphotriester methods are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Very mature with 40 years of impact, so recognition is late rather than early. The long gap and the instrument versus chemistry question are the main concerns.
uncertainties: Contributions of Beaucage, Letsinger and the phosphotriester school are not on the supplied credit list
Whether a one-person award is adequate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological principle, using small molecules to recruit E3 ligases and tag proteins for destruction. It is chemically creative, bridging chemistry and biology, and is in clinical development with growing evidence. The thalidomide cereblon mechanism supplies a striking mechanistic story.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli advanced the VHL ligand and structure-based design. Handa and Ito (cereblon) and Gray, Sakamoto and Kim also have strong claims, so a fair configuration is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Concept validated, but clinical proof is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat premature. As a border field, I ask what is new chemically beyond the biology, and the chemistry is largely linker and ligand design.
uncertainties: Many credible contributors including the cereblon discoverers
